title: Crispy Baked Chicken Wings with Fries
subtitle: wing-night wings baked crisp in the oven, tossed in sticky honey garlic sauce, with a tray of fries
imageAlt: Sticky honey garlic chicken wings piled beside golden fries on a cream plate with a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

breakdown: Soy sauce, garlic, baking powder, spices

beforeYouStart.text: Thaw frozen wings in the fridge overnight and pat them very dry; wet wings won't crisp.
Use plain baking powder, not baking soda. It's the trick for crisp skin without frying.

items.name: chicken wings
items.note: split into flats and drumettes, tips removed

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F) with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Pat the wings very dry and toss with the baking powder, salt, garlic powder and pepper.

steps.title: Bake the wings
steps.text: Spread them skin side up on a rack set in a foil-lined baking sheet, not touching. Bake on the upper rack 45–50 minutes, turning at 25 minutes, until deep golden, crisp and 74°C (165°F) at the thickest part.

steps.title: Fries
steps.text: With 25 minutes left, spread the fries on a second sheet on the lower rack and bake as the package says, turning once. Salt them hot.

steps.title: Sauce
steps.text: Melt the butter in a small pot over medium, cook the garlic 1 minute, then add the honey and soy sauce and bubble 2 minutes until slightly syrupy.

steps.title: Toss
steps.text: Toss the hot wings in a big bowl with the sauce and serve right away with the fries.

fixIt.fix: The wings were wet or crowded. Bake 5–10 minutes more on the top rack, spaced apart.
Bubble it 1–2 minutes more; it thickens as it cools.
Use a rack, or oiled foil, and let them crisp before turning.

saleTip: Fresh wings go on sale in No Frills family packs around big game days; they freeze well flat in a bag.
swap: Party wings already split save time. Air fryer: 200°C for 22–25 minutes in batches, shaking halfway, to 74°C (165°F).
leftovers: Reheat on a rack so they crisp up again.
doneness: Chicken wings at 74°C (165°F) at the thickest part, not touching bone (Health Canada, poultry pieces).
source: Based on tested oven-crisp wing methods (Serious Eats, Canadian Living): dried wings tossed in baking powder and salt, baked on a rack at 220°C, then sauced.
prepAhead: Season the wings with the baking powder mix and leave them uncovered on the rack in the fridge up to 24 hours; they crisp even more.
Make the sauce up to 5 days ahead and warm it before tossing.
reheat: On a rack at 200°C (400°F) for 10 minutes, or the air fryer at 190°C for 6 minutes, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Crispy salt-and-garlic wings with fries; no sauce.

stepNotes.4: Basic: serve the wings straight from the oven.

fancy.note: Half the wings honey garlic, half garlic Parmesan.

addSteps.title: Garlic Parmesan
addSteps.text: Toss half the hot wings in the melted butter and garlic powder, then the Parmesan, before saucing the rest with honey garlic.

plating: Two piles of wings on a board, one of each flavour.
A stack of napkins and a bowl for bones.

why.0-1: Baking powder raises the skin's pH so it browns and blisters like fried skin.
why.1-0: Honey turns glossy and sticky in seconds over the heat.
why.0-0: A rack lets the fat drip away and the hot air reach underneath.

funFact: Buffalo wings were first served in 1964 at the Anchor Bar in Buffalo, New York; before that, wings mostly went into stock.
airFryer: Air-fry the seasoned wings in one layer at 200°C (400°F) for 22–26 minutes, shaking every 8 minutes, until crisp and 74°C (165°F); do 2 batches. Toss in the sauce right away. Frozen fries take 15–18 minutes at 200°C (400°F), shaken twice.
